CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission (trunk/magistral line moving gas condensate-field output ~1,300-1,400 km to a coastal LNG plant) are both correct per energypolicy.ru and interfax.ru. DUPLICATE CHECK against the given 32-row r1-fareast roster: this line is functionally and geographically unrelated to the 8-row Sakhatransneftegaz Srednevilyuyskoye-Yakutsk family (P2334/P3361/P3364/P3365/P6691/P6694/P6695/P6696) even though those rows share some of the same upstream gas condensate fields (Srednevilyuiskoye/Mastakhskoye) as sources -- P3896 is a separate, much longer, not-yet-built corridor running EAST to the Sea of Okhotsk coast (Ayan), while the Sakhatransneftegaz family runs to Yakutsk and other in-republic consumers. First point (122.76 E, 63.90 N) sits almost exactly on Kysyl-Syr settlement in Vilyuysky District, Sakha Republic; last point (138.17 E, 56.45 N) sits almost exactly on Ayan village on the Sea of Okhotsk coast, Khabarovsk Krai -- both termini correctly represent the named project (Kysyl-Syr start, Ayan end), consistent with sudact.ru's routing description (through 6 districts of Yakutia and 2 districts of Khabarovsk Krai). validity.recommendation: Change Capacity from 28.00 to 20.00 bcm/y. The sheet's 28 bcm/y figure is an aggregate FIELD/PRODUCTION target, not this pipeline's designed transport throughput (aggregate-vs-segment rule).
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current ref (sudact.ru) does NOT actually say 28 bcm/y for this pipeline -- its exact text for this project (entry #365 in Annex 4.1 of Decree 816-r) is 'проектный объем транспортировки газа - 20 млрд. куб. метров в год' (design gas TRANSPORT volume = 20 bcm/y). Independently, Interfax (2024-03-27, citing the same federal territorial-planning document) states verbatim: 'проектный объем транспортировки газа составит 20 млрд кубометров в год' (transport) immediately followed, in the same article, by a SEPARATE sentence citing Globaltek's own website: 'ежегодная добыча газа превысит 28 млрд куб. метров' (annual gas PRODUCTION/extraction will exceed 28 bcm). This is a clean, explicit, same-source contrast between two different metrics -- 20 bcm/y is the pipeline's designed transport capacity, 28 bcm/y is the upstream field production target feeding it (and possibly other offtake). The sheet has mapped the production figure into the pipeline Capacity cell. Two independent sources (a primary federal planning document + an independent wire service explicitly contrasting the two numbers) support 20 bcm/y as the correct SEGMENT-level transport capacity; tier high.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newer-than-LastUpdated evidence (LastUpdated=2025-08-15) requires a status change, not merely a confirm. On 2025-10-29, YATEK (Albert Avdolyan's Yakutsk Fuel and Energy Company) announced it has paused/frozen the entire 'Yakutsk LNG' project -- the 17.7 Mtpa LNG plant AND this feeder pipeline, per Kommersant's explicit description of the pipeline as the cost driver ('...потребовало бы строительства крайне дорогого трубопровода длиной 1,3 тыс. км...') -- and pivoted strategy toward gas monetization via data centers/mining/cloud computing. Cause: Globaltek (the project SPV) was placed on the US OFAC SDN List in Feb 2024, which severely complicated equipment supply, trading and financing; combined with high projected LNG cost (driven substantially by this long, expensive pipeline). Independent named expert Alexander Sobko (quoted by Kommersant) corroborates the decision as unsurprising given SDN-driven financing/equipment difficulties. A second, independent outlet (Lenta.ru, same date) reports the same freeze. This is a directly confirmed, dated announcement (not silence-based dormancy inference), so ShelvedCancelledType='confirmed' per the controlled vocabulary, not 'inferred'. Per the dormancy rules, 'shelved' (not yet 'cancelled') is the correct GEM term: the company is not describing this as a permanent cancellation, but as a strategic pause/reallocation -- no source states the project is formally cancelled or abandoned outright, and YATEK explicitly frames it as ceasing to pursue the CURRENT approach, while remaining a producing company with growing reserves (774.4 bcm audited, up from 635 bcm in 2024) that could in principle revisit gas monetization via pipeline+LNG later. If Status is changed to shelved, the now-moot StartYear1=2027 and any FID timeline should be reviewed by a future Update pass, but that is a separate cell-level fix already flagged above, not part of this status verdict.
